Part of `src/lib.rs` (`lib` binary/module).

<!-- TODO: describe what these functions do, and, where relevant, which Fortran subroutine/statement they port. -->

## What this does

Plumbing, not part of the method itself. Builds up the master, sorted list
of distinct site or species codes seen so far as records are read in one
at a time — this is how the programs learn the full set of sites/species
in a data set without being told it in advance. `addwrd_guarded` is the
same thing but stops (silently) once a fixed array-size limit is reached,
matching the original Fortran's static array bounds.

### `addwrd`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__addwrd"}
pub fn addwrd(sa: &mut [Name], m: &mut usize, samp: &Name) {
    let i = if *m == 0 { 0 } else { binfnd(sa, *m, samp) };
    if i != 0 {
        return;
    }
    *m += 1;
    sa[*m] = *samp;
    sa[1..=*m].sort_unstable();
}
```

### `addwrd_guarded`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__addwrd_guarded"}
pub fn addwrd_guarded(sa: &mut [Name], mm: usize, m: &mut usize, samp: &Name) {
    let i = if *m == 0 { 0 } else { binfnd(sa, *m, samp) };
    if i != 0 {
        return;
    }
    *m += 1;
    if *m > mm {
        return;
    }
    sa[*m] = *samp;
    sa[1..=*m].sort_unstable();
}
```
